answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each account to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit work, then randomly auditing claims against independently verified outcomes. If an audit finds fabricated identities or collusive results, the protocol slashes that stake; honest agents recover it after the challenge period. This makes each fake account require real capital, and detection imposes a direct loss, so multiplying identities is costly rather than free. A sonnet, an oasis, or a marble may be cheap to invent as a persona, but none supplies the stake or survives verification.
